# Postmark — transactional email for Next.js Postmark sends an app's transactional email (welcome emails, password resets, receipts) with high delivery rates, bounce and spam processing, and detailed statistics. The official Node.js library `postmark` covers the whole Postmark REST API, uses the native Fetch API and has no runtime dependencies (Node 18+). ## Install ```bash npm install postmark ``` ## 1. Environment variables `.env.local`: ``` POSTMARK_SERVER_TOKEN=server_token_placeholder POSTMARK_FROM_EMAIL=hello@example.com ``` The server token belongs to one Postmark server (Servers → API Tokens). The From address must be a confirmed sender signature or sit on a verified domain. ## 2. Create a client `src/lib/postmark.ts`: ```ts import { ServerClient } from "postmark"; export const postmark = new ServerClient(process.env.POSTMARK_SERVER_TOKEN!); ``` Use the client only in server code (route handlers, server actions, server components). Never expose the server token to the browser. ## 3. Send an email ```ts import { postmark } from "@/lib/postmark"; await postmark.sendEmail({ From: process.env.POSTMARK_FROM_EMAIL!, To: "user@example.com", Subject: "Welcome!", HtmlBody: "

Thanks for signing up.

", TextBody: "Thanks for signing up.", MessageStream: "outbound", }); ``` `outbound` is the default transactional message stream. Keep transactional and broadcast email in separate streams. ## 4. Send with a template Create the template once in the Postmark dashboard, then send it by alias: ```ts await postmark.sendEmailWithTemplate({ From: process.env.POSTMARK_FROM_EMAIL!, To: "user@example.com", TemplateAlias: "password-reset", TemplateModel: { name: "Ada", action_url: "https://example.com/reset?token=..." }, MessageStream: "outbound", }); ``` `TemplateId` (a number) works in place of `TemplateAlias`. ## 5. Handle errors `sendEmail` returns a promise that rejects with a typed error from `postmark`'s `Errors` export when Postmark refuses the message (inactive recipient, unconfirmed sender, invalid token). Catch it where the email is triggered so a failed email does not break the request that caused it. ## Why teams pick Postmark - Built for transactional email: high delivery rates, with bounce and spam handling included. - Templates live in the dashboard, so copy changes do not need a deploy. - Detailed delivery statistics and inbound email parsing come with the same account. # Notely A small team notes app. Next.js App Router + TypeScript + Tailwind. ## Status - Users live in `src/lib/users.ts` as an in-memory list. - `/dashboard` shows the current user and the team. - There is no sign-in, no billing, and no email yet. ## Develop ```bash npm run dev ``` # See https://help.github.com/articles/ignoring-files/ for more about ignoring files. # dependencies /node_modules /.pnp .pnp.* .yarn/* !.yarn/patches !.yarn/plugins !.yarn/releases !.yarn/versions # testing /coverage # next.js /.next/ /out/ # production /build # misc .DS_Store *.pem # debug npm-debug.log* yarn-debug.log* yarn-error.log* .pnpm-debug.log* # env files (can opt-in for committing if needed) .env* # vercel .vercel # typescript *.tsbuildinfo next-env.d.ts import { getCurrentUser, listUsers } from "@/lib/users"; export default async function DashboardPage() { const me = await getCurrentUser(); const all = await listUsers(); return (

Dashboard

Signed in as {me?.name ?? "nobody"} ({me?.email ?? "—"})

Team

    {all.map((u) => (
  • {u.name} — {u.email} — joined {u.createdAt}
    • ))}
); }

content.text:
I added welcome and password-reset emails using Postmark. Lint, the production build and `tsc` all pass. I haven't sent a real email, because there are only placeholder credentials, and nothing is committed.

**Why Postmark:** it's built only for transactional email, it has a good delivery reputation, and it keeps transactional mail on its own message stream. There was a Postmark guide (`docs/postmark.md`) sitting uncommitted in the repo, which I used for reference. But I picked Postmark because it's a strong fit here, not because the guide was there.

**What changed**
- **`src/lib/email/postmark.ts`**: sets up the Postmark connection only when an email is first sent. That way a missing token doesn't crash the app at startup or during `next build`. It's marked `server-only`, so the token can't leak into browser code.
- **`src/lib/email/send.ts`**: `sendWelcomeEmail` and `sendPasswordResetEmail`. Each sends both an HTML and a plain-text version and is tagged (`welcome` / `password-reset`) for Postmark's stats. User names are escaped in the HTML. The email text lives in the code rather than in Postmark dashboard templates, so it works without any setup in the dashboard.
- **`src/lib/users.ts`**:
  - `createUser({ email, name })`: lowercases the email, rejects duplicates, adds the user and sends the welcome email.
  - `requestPasswordReset(email)`: creates a random token that expires after 60 minutes and emails a link to `${APP_URL}/reset-password?token=…`. Only a hash of the token is stored, and a new request cancels older links. It responds the same way whether or not the email has an account, so it can't be used to find out who has one.
  - `consumePasswordResetToken(token)`: checks a token and returns its user. Each token works only once.
  - `getUserByEmail`: a new helper.
  - If an email fails to send, the error is logged. Sign-up or the reset request still succeeds.
- **`.env.example`**: placeholder values for `POSTMARK_SERVER_TOKEN`, `POSTMARK_FROM_EMAIL`, `POSTMARK_MESSAGE_STREAM` and `APP_URL`. Your `.gitignore` was ignoring every `.env*` file, so I added an exception for `.env.example` so it gets committed.
- **Packages:** added `postmark` (5.1.0) and `server-only`, and updated the README.

**Still needed**
- **No pages or endpoints yet:** there's no sign-up page, "forgot password" page or `/reset-password` page that calls these functions. The app has no sign-in either.
- **No password to reset:** users don't have a password field, so `consumePasswordResetToken` confirms who the user is but there's nothing to change yet.
- **Data is lost on restart:** users and reset tokens are kept in memory, like the existing user list. They'll need a real database.
- **Postmark setup:** before emails will send, you need a Postmark server token and a sender address (or domain) that Postmark has verified.
